source: NCERT Class VII, Our Pasts II, History Ch. 7.

sections.heading: 1. Beyond Big Cities — Tribes
points: Not everyone lived in caste-based (**varna**) society; many people lived in **tribes**.
**Tribes** were united by **kinship**; they did not follow the varna order; often lived in **forests, hills, deserts** and practised **farming, herding or hunting-gathering**.
Tribes usually had **oral traditions** (little written record), so we learn about them from **outsiders' accounts** and their own memories.

sections.heading: 2. Nomads and Mobile People
points: **Nomadic pastoralists** moved with their animals, living on **milk and other produce**, and exchanged **wool, ghee** etc. for grain, cloth and utensils.
The **Banjaras** were the most important **trader-nomads** — their caravan = **tanda**; they carried **grain** for armies and towns.
Some mobile groups were **entertainers, peddlers and craftspeople** moving town to town.

sections.heading: 3. Changing Society — New Castes and Mobility
points: As society grew, many **jatis (sub-castes)** emerged based on occupation; some tribes became part of **caste society**, often at a **low rank**.
Some powerful tribes founded **kingdoms**; **Brahmanas** then gave them **kshatriya** status and genealogies.
Thus tribal and caste societies constantly **influenced each other**.

sections.heading: 4. Important Tribal Kingdoms
points: **Gonds** (Gondwana, central India) — practised **shifting cultivation**; the **Garha Katanga** kingdom; **Rani Durgawati** resisted the Mughals.

**Ahoms** (Assam) — migrated from Myanmar (13th c.); built a strong state; suppressed older political systems (**bhuiyans**); used **firearms** and had a **paik** (forced labour) system; wrote **buranjis** (chronicles).
**Bhils** (western/central India) and **Santhals** were other large tribes.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Tribes = kinship-based, outside varna society; mostly oral records.
Banjaras = trader-nomads; caravan = tanda; carried grain.
Gonds = Gondwana, shifting cultivation, Garha Katanga; Rani Durgawati fought the Mughals.
Ahoms = Assam; buranjis (chronicles); paik (forced labour) system.
Powerful tribes became kingdoms; Brahmanas granted them kshatriya status.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Banjaras** (tanda caravans) were the main grain-carrying **trader-nomads**.
**Ahoms** = Assam; their chronicles are the **buranjis**.
**Gonds** lived in **Gondwana** and practised **shifting cultivation**; Rani Durgawati (Garha Katanga) resisted **Akbar's** general.
Tribes were **kinship-based** and generally outside the **varna/jati** hierarchy.
